column1: # doc-cap-cases.tsv — THE truth table for the document size cap, and the only copy.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The cap rule is implemented TWICE, in two languages, with no compiler between
# them:
#   server/ocserverd/domain.go      DocCapBlocked      — the AUTHORITY. It is
#                                   what actually refuses a write (HTTP 400).
#   frontend/src/api/docCap.ts      docCapBlocked      — a stand-in, so the
#                                   cockpit can mark a revision un-restorable
#                                   BEFORE the owner clicks it.
# The frontend copy is temporary: once DocumentHistoryDTO carries a per-revision
# `restorable` + `reason` (a frozen-wire change, blocked on owner approval) it is
# deleted and this table loses its only reader. Until then a drift does not
# produce an error anywhere — it produces a cockpit that LIES: a row shown as
# restorable that the server refuses, or worse, a perfectly good revision greyed
# out with a reason that is not true. Neither side would notice.
# Only the TS side is checked against THIS table:
#   frontend/src/api/docCap.test.ts
# Nothing in Go reads it, so a drift in DocCapBlocked reddens nothing here.
# THE RULE (both sides, boundaries included)
#   after ≤ cap                    → allowed
#   after > cap AND after < before → allowed  (an over-cap doc may converge down)
#   after > cap AND after ≥ before → REFUSED  (equal length included)
# THE UNIT IS UNICODE CODE POINTS (runes) — not bytes, not UTF-16 units. Go says
# utf8.RuneCountInString; TypeScript must say [...s].length, because
# String.length counts UTF-16 units and double-counts every astral character.
# The `astral-*` and `cjk-*` rows below are the ones that make that difference
# observable: they are engineered so that a byte count or a UTF-16 count gives
# the OPPOSITE verdict to the rune count. If a test only carries ASCII rows,
# swapping the unit passes silently — which is the whole reason those rows exist.
# cap<TAB><n> below is read by both tests, so the threshold is not a third copy.
# cap
# COLUMNS  case<TAB>before_runes<TAB>after_runes<TAB>blocked<TAB>fill
#   case          row name, used in failure messages
#   before_runes  length of the CURRENT stored document, in runes
#   after_runes   length of the PROPOSED replacement, in runes
#   blocked       expected verdict: true = the server refuses the write
#   fill          the single code point both strings are built by repeating.
#                 This column is what gives the table discriminating power: with
#                 lengths alone, every row is ASCII and the unit cannot be
#                 tested at all.
case
empty-both
first-write-small
under-cap
at-cap-exactly
first-write-over-cap
over-cap-growing
over-cap-equal
over-cap-one-more
over-cap-shrinking
over-cap-shrinking-to-cap
cjk-under-cap-in-runes-over-in-bytes
cjk-over-cap
astral-under-cap-in-runes-over-in-utf16
astral-over-cap
astral-over-cap-shrinking
